## Proof

**Setup.** We construct the modified Cantor set $C_\alpha$ as follows. Start with $C_0 = [0,1]$. At each step $n \geq 1$, from every closed interval $I$ of length $|I|$ currently present, remove the open middle interval of length $\alpha |I|$ (where $0 < \alpha < 1$). This leaves two closed sub-intervals, each of length

$$\frac{|I| - \alpha|I|}{2} = \frac{1-\alpha}{2}\,|I|.$$

Define $C_n$ as the union of all intervals remaining after step $n$, and $C_\alpha = \bigcap_{n=0}^{\infty} C_n$.

**Counting the intervals and their lengths.** At step $n$, the construction produces $2^n$ closed intervals. By the recurrence above, each has length

$$\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\right)^n.$$

**Total length (Lebesgue measure) of $C_n$.** Since the $2^n$ intervals are pairwise disjoint,

$$m(C_n) = 2^n \cdot \left(\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\right)^n = (1-\alpha)^n.$$

**Taking the limit.** Because $0 < \alpha < 1$, we have $0 < 1-\alpha < 1$, and therefore

$$\lim_{n \to \infty} (1-\alpha)^n = 0.$$

The sets $C_n$ are nested ($C_0 \supseteq C_1 \supseteq C_2 \supseteq \cdots$) and each has finite measure ($m(C_0)=1$). By continuity of measure from above,

$$m(C_\alpha) = m\!\left(\bigcap_{n=0}^{\infty} C_n\right) = \lim_{n \to \infty} m(C_n) = \lim_{n \to \infty}(1-\alpha)^n = 0.$$

**Conclusion.** For every $0 < \alpha < 1$, the modified Cantor set $C_\alpha$ has Lebesgue measure zero. The key point is that the total remaining length at step $n$ is $(1-\alpha)^n$, which tends to $0$ whenever $\alpha > 0$. (When $\alpha = 0$, nothing is removed and $m(C_0)=1$; this is the excluded degenerate case.) $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
